info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package code is search and symbols across your repos, for you and your agents.

get.summary: Answers a question about the caller org's code with a CITED answer: retrieval packs grounding context, then the synthesizer writes the answer over exactly those spans, which come back alongside it.
get.description:
Answers a question about the caller org's code with a CITED answer:
retrieval packs grounding context, then the synthesizer writes the answer over
exactly those spans, which come back alongside it. It never answers without
grounding — with no matched code the answer is empty and says so, and with no
synthesizer available the citations still come back with "degraded": true so
the caller can reason over the spans itself.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Q is the question to answer. Required, max 4000 bytes.
parameters.example: where is the per-org SQLite file opened

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description:
Repo narrows retrieval to one repository. Empty searches every repo the org
has indexed.

post.summary: Is askGet with the question in the request BODY, for a question too long or too awkward to put in a URL.
post.description:
Is askGet with the question in the request BODY, for a question too
long or too awkward to put in a URL. `query` and `repo` in the body take
precedence over `?q=` and `?repo=`; either source works alone.

example.query: where is the per-org SQLite file opened

post.summary: Packs the most relevant code for a query into a token budget — THE primitive for a coding agent that has to decide what to put in a prompt.
post.description:
Packs the most relevant code for a query into a token budget — THE
primitive for a coding agent that has to decide what to put in a prompt. It
retrieves seed spans, expands each with the definitions it calls and its key
callers, then greedily fills the budget, so the answer is a coherent slice of
the codebase rather than a list of disconnected matches. The top match is
always included, truncated if it alone overflows, so a matched query never
comes back empty. A retrieval outage answers 200 with an empty bundle rather
than a 5xx.

example.query: how does the store open a per-org database

get.summary: Returns the INDEXED content of one file — read_file over the chunks the search tiers hold, for pulling up code an agent just found.
get.description:
Returns the INDEXED content of one file — read_file over the chunks the
search tiers hold, for pulling up code an agent just found. It is NOT
byte-verbatim: the git object plane is the source of record for exact bytes,
history and blame. A file absent from the index is a 404, so an agent can tell
"not indexed" from "empty file".

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path is the file's repo-relative path. Required.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repo is the repository the file belongs to. REQUIRED.

post.summary: (re)indexes a repository for the caller's org, incrementally: files whose content hash is unchanged are skipped, so re-sending a whole tree is cheap.
post.description:
(re)indexes a repository for the caller's org, incrementally: files whose
content hash is unchanged are skipped, so re-sending a whole tree is cheap.
Each file is parsed for symbols, split at AST boundaries and — when the
semantic tier is available — embedded, which is what makes it searchable across
all three retrieval tiers. Pass `prune` to also DELETE indexed files absent
from the request, which turns the call into a full sync; without it the call is
an upsert. The index is written to the caller org's own physically separate
database.

get.summary: Finds code in the caller org's index across three orthogonal retrieval tiers fused by reciprocal-rank fusion: lexical (FTS5 trigram over code-tokenized text), symbolic (real definition and reference edges), and semantic (embedding cosine over AST-boundary chunks).
get.description:
Finds code in the caller org's index across three orthogonal retrieval
tiers fused by reciprocal-rank fusion: lexical (FTS5 trigram over
code-tokenized text), symbolic (real definition and reference edges), and
semantic (embedding cosine over AST-boundary chunks). Pick one tier with
`type`, or leave it to run all three as hybrid, which is what a coding agent
usually wants. It is FAIL-HONEST: a retrieval outage answers 200 with an empty
result set and "degraded": true rather than a 5xx, so an agent degrades instead
of stalling. A malformed regex is a 400.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Q is the search query. Required, max 4000 bytes. For type=regex it is a
regular expression; for type=symbol it is a symbol name.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
Type selects the retrieval tier: "text" (FTS5 trigram), "regex",
"symbol" (definitions), "semantic" (embeddings) or "hybrid". Anything
else — including empty — reads as hybrid.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repo narrows to one repository. Empty searches every repo the org has indexed.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit caps how many spans come back: default 20, maximum 100. A value that
is not a positive integer reads as the default.

get.summary: Returns one repository's file structure with a per-file symbol count — get_repo_structure over the org's own index, with no git checkout involved.
get.description:
Returns one repository's file structure with a per-file symbol count —
get_repo_structure over the org's own index, with no git checkout involved. A
repository that has not been indexed answers an empty tree rather than an
error, so an agent can tell "nothing here" without handling a failure.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repo is the repository to walk. REQUIRED — a tree is repo-scoped.

answer.description:
Answer is the synthesized prose. EMPTY is a real answer here: nothing in the
index matched, or synthesis was unavailable — read `degraded` and `citations`
to tell those apart. It is never written without grounding.

citations.description:
Citations are the exact regions the answer was grounded on, and they are the
point: an answer is checkable only because every claim in it can be read back
at a file and line. Present even when Answer is empty.

degraded.description:
Degraded is true when retrieval worked but no synthesizer was reachable. The
citations are still real code, so a caller can answer from them itself; a
caller that treats this like an error throws away a usable result.

question.description: Question is the ask, echoed back.

endLine.description: EndLine is its last line, inclusive.

file.description: File is the path inside the repo, relative to its root.

line.description: Line is the first line of the cited region, 1-based.

repo.description:
Repo is the repository the cited code lives in ("owner/name"), absent when the
ask was already scoped to one.

symbol.description: Symbol is the declaration the region belongs to, when it belongs to one.

budgetTokens.description:
BudgetTokens is the ceiling the caller asked for. Packing stops under it, so
this is a bound and not a target.

query.description:
Query is the ask this bundle was packed for, echoed back so a cached or
forwarded bundle still says what it answers.

repo.description:
Repo narrows the retrieval to one repository. Absent means every indexed repo
was searched.

spans.description:
Spans are the packed chunks, most relevant first, each expanded with the
definitions it calls and its notable callers. The top match is always present
even if it had to be truncated to fit, so a matched query never comes back
with nothing.

usedTokens.description:
UsedTokens is what the returned spans actually cost, by the same estimate the
packer used (roughly one token per four characters — an estimate, not a
tokenizer's count, so size a real window with headroom).

endLine.description:
EndLine is the last line of the span, inclusive. It equals Line for a
one-line span rather than being zero or absent.

file.description: File is the path inside the repo, relative to its root and never absolute.

kind.description:
Kind is what the indexer decided this chunk IS — "func", "method", "type",
"struct", "interface", "var", "const", or "block" for a run of code that
declares nothing. Absent when the chunker could not classify it.

line.description: Line is where the span starts, 1-based, as an editor counts.

repo.description:
Repo is the indexed repository the span was found in, as it was indexed
("owner/name"). A search may be scoped to one repo or run across all of them,
so this is how a caller tells the results apart.

score.description:
Score ranks this span against the OTHERS IN THE SAME RESPONSE and means
nothing across responses or between tiers: the hybrid tier's number is a
reciprocal-rank fusion sum (Σ 1/(60+rank), so tenths at best), the symbol
tier's is a descending position count, and the text and semantic tiers pass
through bm25 and cosine. Compare within a list; never threshold on it.

snippet.description:
Snippet is the code itself: a bounded excerpt on /search, the whole chunk on
/context — which is why the same type serves both and why a /context span is
the one an agent pastes into its window.

symbol.description: Symbol is the declared name, when the span declares one. Absent on a block.

tier.description:
Tier is which retrieval produced the span: "hybrid" (the default — all three
fused), "text" (trigram/FTS), "regex", "semantic" (vector), or "symbol". It is
what explains a Score, so the two travel together.

lang.description:
Lang is the language the indexer parsed the file as ("go", "python", …), or
empty when it recognised none — in which case Symbols is 0 because nothing was
extracted, not because the file declares nothing.

path.description:
Path is the file, relative to the repo root. The list is ordered by it, so a
reader can see module layout without sorting.

symbols.description:
Symbols is how many top-level declarations the file defines. A file with none
is still listed: the file set is the authority here and the counts decorate it.

query.description: Query is the question, from the BODY. Takes precedence over `?q=`.

repo.description: Repo is the repository narrowing, from the BODY. Takes precedence over `?repo=`.

budgetTokens.description:
BudgetTokens caps the bundle's size. Clamped to [256, 32000]; 0 or absent
uses 4000.

query.description: Query is what to retrieve context for. Required, max 4000 bytes.

repo.description:
Repo narrows retrieval to one repository. Empty searches every repo the org
has indexed.

content.description:
Content is the file's text as the index stored it. It is NOT guaranteed
byte-verbatim — the git object plane is the source of record for exact
bytes, history and blame.

path.description: Path echoes the file that was read.

repo.description: Repo echoes the repository it came from.

content.description:
Content is the file's full text. Max 1 MiB per file; binary files should
simply be omitted rather than sent.

path.description: Path is the file's repo-relative path, e.g. "internal/store/db.go".

files.description:
Files is the full set of files to index. Required and non-empty; max 20000
files, 1 MiB per file and 1 GiB in total. Unchanged files are skipped by
content hash, so re-sending the whole tree is cheap.

prune.description:
Prune deletes indexed files that are NOT in this request — which makes the
call a full sync of the repo rather than an upsert. Only pass it when Files
is the complete tree.

repo.description:
Repo is the repository label to index under. Required, max 200 bytes. It is
a stored column value, not a filesystem path.

chunks.description: Chunks is how many AST-boundary chunks the repo holds after this pass.

files.description: Files is how many files the repo holds after this pass.

indexed.description: Indexed is how many files were parsed and written on this pass.

pruned.description:
Pruned is how many stored files were deleted because prune was set and they
were absent from the request.

repo.description: Repo is the repository that was indexed.

semantic.description:
Semantic reports whether the semantic tier was available for this pass. When
false the index is lexical + symbolic only and hybrid search still works.

skipped.description: Skipped is how many files were unchanged by content hash and left alone.

symbols.description: Symbols is how many symbol definitions the repo holds after this pass.

vectors.description: Vectors is how many of those chunks carry an embedding.

files.description:
Files are the repo's indexed files in path order, each with its language
and how many symbols it defines. Never null.

repo.description: Repo echoes the repository that was walked.

degraded.description:
Degraded is true when retrieval failed and the empty result set is an
outage rather than a real absence of matches. Absent on a healthy answer.

query.description: Query echoes the query that was run.

results.description:
Results are the matching spans, best first. Never null — an empty search is
an empty array.

type.description: Type echoes the retrieval tier that ran, after defaulting.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
